title: Actual reconstruction maps for normalized strict systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. On a fixed small skeleton of its pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], put $B_{n,W}=(R/\varpi^n)_W$ and $\widehat R_W=\varprojlim_n B_{n,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear $B_{n,W}$-module systems, with componentwise morphisms, of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and use its unbounded derived category. Write $\mathscr N_W$ for the full subcategory with all transition adjoints $N_m\otimes^L_{B_{m,W}}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ invertible for $m\ge n$, and $\mathscr C_W\subset D(\widehat R_W)$ for the full subcategory of derived-complete complexes [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower, def-weil-derived-complete]. No cohomological bound, constructibility, uniform Tor interval or equipped local model is assumed.

Use the specified adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ U_W$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], with its actual unit $u$ and counit $e$. Then $\mathcal R_W(P)$ is normalized for every ambient $P\in D(\widehat R_W)$. For every normalized $N\in D(\mathscr S_W)$, $\mathcal L_WN$ is derived complete and the actual map $e_N:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WN\to N$ is an isomorphism of derived strict systems. At every level $n$, its evaluation is the scalar-extension adjoint $(\mathcal L_WN)\otimes^L_{\widehat R_W}B_{n,W}\to N_n$ of the specified total-limit projection. For every derived-complete $K$, the actual unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_W\mathcal R_WK$ is an isomorphism. These maps are natural in $N$ and $K$, with the triangle identities of the specified adjunction; there are no boundedness, constructibility or Tor-amplitude hypotheses.

proof.text: For any strict system, its restricted tower has the canonical Roos triangle. The zero composition of consecutive arrows in that triangle proves compatibility of its total-limit projections with successor transitions. Transport through the restricted-evaluation comparison. Precompose by the reconstruction unit and use unit_projection. Taking finite scalar-extension adjoints identifies the transitions of reduction(K), under reductionEvaluation, with normalizedDVRReductionTransition.

proof.text: Unpack derived completeness of K into its K-flat resolution q:P→G, representative isomorphism and canonical quotient Roos triangle. The invertible K-flat scalar comparison identifies the restricted finite reductions of K with the localized strict quotients of P. The previous transition identity and normalizedDVR_kflat_transition make these identifications commute with successive transitions. Transport the canonical total-limit Roos triangle along their product. Thus K and L R K are derived limits of the same strict quotient tower.

proof.text: Uniqueness up to isomorphism of the objects of Roos triangles gives an isomorphism φ:K≅L R K. It need not be the actual adjunction unit. Since e_(RK) is invertible, the right triangle identity makes u_(LRK) invertible. Naturality at φ gives φ≫u_(LRK)=u_K≫LR(φ); cancellation of the two isomorphisms makes the actual u_K invertible. This avoids identifying maps into a homotopy limit by their projections.

lean.statement:
theorem purNormalizedReconstruction
    (_hl : IsUnit (l : Γ(W, ⊤))) (S : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E W) :
    (∀ (N : coefficientSequenceDerived l E W), IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence l E W N →
      IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E W none ((coefficientSequenceLimit l E W).obj N) ∧
        IsIso (S.adjunction.counit.app N)) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource l E W)),
      IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E W none K → IsIso (S.adjunction.unit.app K))
lean.note: Existing reconstruction theorem for the very specified CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus adjunction: completeness of the normalized total limit and invertibility of its actual counit, and invertibility of its actual unit on complete objects. The remaining explicit clauses are already fields of its input calculus: reduction_normalized and counit_projection, with naturality and both triangle identities in S.adjunction. No replacement maps, boundedness, finite-field datum or Tor hypotheses are introduced. See the worker report for every clause and the positive-level indexing convention.
